en.alert.hint.connect_refused: TCP refused (proxy when configured, else upstream) — endpoint down or wrong port
en.alert.hint.connect_timeout: TCP handshake never completed — upstream/proxy unreachable or blackholed; a bounded transparent replay may be attempted (BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_MAX)
en.alert.hint.dns: name resolution failed — DNS server or hostname typo; a bounded transparent replay may be attempted (BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_MAX)
en.alert.hint.proxy_reset: proxy dropped the connection before the response — check proxy idle-recycle/payload limits (BILI_PROXY_KEEPALIVE_MAX_MS can shorten our reuse window); a bounded transparent replay may be attempted (BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_MAX)
en.alert.hint.tls: TLS/certificate failure at CONNECT or upstream handshake — CA/proxy MITM config
en.alert.hint.unknown: unclassified transport failure — report with full error chain
en.alert.hint.upstream_reset: upstream/network reset before the response — check upstream and local network; a bounded transparent replay may be attempted (BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_MAX)
en.alert.note.skipped_proxy: available proxy {proxy} ({source}) was skipped — upstreamProxyMode is unset (direct is the default by design, #346/#357); set "upstreamProxyMode": "auto" or BILI_UPSTREAM_PROXY_MODE=auto, or give this provider a "proxy" lane to enable it

en.cfg.file_desc: This card edits the config file directly — every top-level field in this JSON takes effect (routes, compression, network, passthrough, promptPack, ccr, …). Saving applies immediately
en.cfg.parse_error: Config file is not valid JSON — showing an empty view
en.cfg.passthrough_desc: Decides whether traffic matching no route passes through to the target service untouched (no interception, no rewriting). State lives in the config file; when forced by the ACP_PASSTHROUGH env var the UI marks the source and you must unset the variable and restart before changing it here
en.cfg.q_absorb: Instant tool-result absorption (absorb) — large tool results are distilled by the model on arrival; originals hidden until the next fold round (default off)
en.cfg.q_absorb_hint: by default only image-bearing results are absorbed (#3422); set mediaOnly: false to absorb full text. Sub-fields (minToolTokens, contextThresholdPct, excludeTools) go in the JSON editor below
en.cfg.q_imgrescale: Outbound image downscale (imageRescale) — large outbound images are shrunken before reaching the model; originals stay in local session storage (default on)
en.cfg.q_never_note: Default excludes decompress, search_context, read, bash — during bulk reads drop read from the list so freshly-read files are not folded immediately
en.cfg.q_never_ph: comma-separated, * globs ok; empty = kernel built-in list (incl. read, bash)
en.cfg.q_nudge_high: above 100000: a very long context between folds may weaken model attention
en.cfg.q_nudge_low: below 20000: folding this often degrades summary quality (kernel default 50000)
en.cfg.q_pack_custom: custom pack — loaded by name from ~/.config/billion-context/packs/ (or project .billion-context/packs/)
en.cfg.q_pack_default_desc: default (full surface): detailed tool descriptions plus complete compression rules — richest guidance. Measured ≈2,900+ tokens per request (qwen tokenizer)
en.cfg.q_pack_lean_desc: lean: one-line tool descriptions, condensed rules — terser guidance. Measured ≈1,400 tokens per request (qwen tokenizer), roughly half of default
en.cfg.q_parse_err: The advanced JSON cannot be parsed right now — quick controls are paused until it is valid again
en.cfg.q_passthrough: Passthrough mode (passthrough) — pure proxying, no injection, no compression
en.cfg.q_ptools_ph: comma-separated, * globs ok, e.g. skill, skill_*; empty by default
en.cfg.q_ptools_warn: Do not protect chatty tools like read / bash / edit — their output dominates most sessions' tokens; protecting them means it is never compressed and context keeps growing
en.cfg.q_tiers: Per-tier compress trigger thresholds tokens (compress.tierNudgeTokens; prefilled with derived defaults, only changed values saved)
en.cfg.q_tiers_desc: Prefilled with the current derived defaults (T1 = growth step, T2/T3 = ×1.5); unchanged values are not saved. Note: T2/T3 count lower-tier SUMMARY tokens, not raw — at the default 75K and a ~10:1 summarization ratio one T2 block carries ~750K raw context; raise T2 for longer projects.
en.cfg.q_tiers_tip_t1: T1 raw-message fold trigger (measured in raw tokens) — default = the compress growth threshold above
en.cfg.q_tiers_tip_t2: T2 re-distill trigger (measured in T1-summary tokens) — default = growth threshold × 1.5; raise it so each T2 block carries more project history
en.cfg.q_tiers_tip_t3: T3 condense trigger (measured in T2-summary tokens) — default = growth threshold × 1.5
en.cfg.quick_desc: Toggle common options without touching JSON — every change syncs live into the raw editor below (same file, no new config fields); advanced structures like the providers table stay in the JSON
en.cfg.resign_awaiting: awaiting re-signer support in bili (per the compress-or-refuse contract, no config can pass this through)
en.cfg.resign_builtin: Built-in scheme {scheme} ({label}): bili re-signs automatically (normal compression) when the dsh credential service resolves; otherwise local refusal
en.cfg.resign_copy_hint: Copy this snippet into the config file: this link forwards byte-untouched WITHOUT compression (built-in scheme only)
en.cfg.resign_desc: Upstreams that sign the request body: any rewrite makes their signature check fail (401). Per the compress-or-refuse contract a signed request has exactly two outcomes — re-signed+compressed, or refused locally (403); there is no unsigned pass-through mode. The built-in scheme may opt into passthrough (explicitly accepting uncompressed forwarding) when no credential resolves; every other scheme stays unavailable until bili ships its re-signer (no config can pass it through). Entries come from signatures observed at runtime
en.cfg.resign_disabled: protection disabled (pre-resign behavior: body is rewritten, upstream may 401)
en.cfg.resign_none: No pending signature refusals — no un-re-signable signed requests observed
en.cfg.state_reached: HTTP {status} · reachable (auth handled by the client)
en.cfg.sub: Edits write straight to the config file and hot-apply · check JSON syntax before saving
en.cfg.test_hint: Sends one minimal request to verify reachability; changes nothing

en.conflict.hint.claude: claude: launch through bili claude (it aligns CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW automatically), or set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW to bili's effective window yourself
en.conflict.hint.codex: codex: bili intercepts native compaction by default (BILI_CODEX_COMPACT=intercept) — if you set pass, remove the override to stop; otherwise report your bili version
en.conflict.hint.generic: disable the client's own auto-compaction (or route this session around bili), then start a fresh session — the ledger is per-session, so old entries clear with the old session
en.conflict.hint.omp: omp: the bili extension cancels the client's native auto-compaction while it carries the conversation — seeing this suggests missing carriage evidence or an old version; report client + bili version
en.conflict.hint.opencode: opencode: set "compaction": { "auto": false } in your opencode config (or use bili opencode / bili plugin install opencode, which set it for you)
en.conflict.hint.pi: pi: the bili extension cancels the client's native auto-compaction while it carries the conversation — seeing this suggests missing carriage evidence or an old version; report client + bili version
en.conflict.risk_active: were found. Two compressors on one conversation double-compress and corrupt message refs, which can scramble context — keep exactly one compressor.
en.conflict.risk_historical: were found (no events in the last 7 days — stock records only) — once you've confirmed the other compressor is removed or blocked by bili, clear them with the button.
en.conflict.risk_sibling: were found. These are bili's OWN sibling extensions, not third-party compressors: while bili drives the session they stand down automatically (BILLION_CONTEXT_NATIVE marker in native mode, /bili/ baseUrl self-check otherwise), so no second compressor is active — verify your versions are recent and clear this record; nothing needs removing.
en.conflict.risk_suspected: — a name-only [suspected] signal, not observed evidence of double-compression. Confirm it actually rewrites the model context before acting; a display / tool-output-folding plugin (e.g. pi-compact-transcript) does not double-compress and needs no removal.
en.conflict.risk_unconfirmed: — all of the above are UNCONFIRMED signals: they do not prove a second compressor exists (possible causes: client-side edits, an unrecognized compaction shape, or another plugin). Verify before acting; a read-only context viewer or a display / tool-output-folding plugin is not a compressor and needs no removal.
en.conflict.what_plugin: a third-party compression plugin co-resident with bili
en.conflict.what_signal: conversation history being rewritten (a change was observed, cause not yet identified)
en.conflict.what_suspected: a plugin whose name matches compression keywords (not yet verified to actually compress context)
en.conflict.where: Details: Sessions page below or the conflicts field of GET /__bili/stats.
en.data.error: Failed to load data: {msg} · auto-retrying with backoff
en.data.generic: network error or request timed out
en.det.attr_abort_tip: Missed samples settled within 30s of a client mid-stream abort — retry churn rewrites the resent tail; correlation, not causation (overlay marker, not a bucket)
en.det.attr_client_tip: The client's own resent history diverged mid-list (insert/rewrite — another host plugin, paste hoisting, re-render): the inbound message-fingerprint pair mismatches at that index, and bili's faithful rebuild carried the change to the wire. Client-owned re-bill, not a bili rebuild seam (#3023)
en.det.attr_provider_tip: Arrived shortly after the previous request, whose entire message list came back byte-identical (whole body, or its prefix with only tail messages appended; above the 512 KiB forensics cap, proven by the stable recorded head plus exact message-count growth) yet the upstream did not serve its cache — abnormal: eviction / relay node rotation. Long-gap siblings are booked under upstream TTL expiry
en.det.attr_rest_tip: small residuals below the classification threshold (<8K or <30% of input per sample), not individually classified
en.det.attr_restart_tip: After a bili restart or session restore the ledger window breaks: the first post-restart request cannot pair with pre-restart samples, so its miss is billed as a first bill (initial content)
en.det.attr_rewind_tip: Client revert/trim shrank the message count — sanctioned one-time re-bill of the retained prefix, not a defect
en.det.attr_seam_tip: Outbound bodies diverged mid-history with no fold/model-switch/restart attribution — suspected rebuild seam. Value = tokens re-billed on suspect samples. If a fold landed minutes earlier this is usually the post-fold client-echo re-bill (fold-owned since #2929)
en.det.attr_ttl_tip: byte-stable / append-shaped misses settled more than 10 minutes after the previous sample — the upstream prefix cache simply aged out; expected cost, no action needed
en.det.auto_mode_forge_local: auto-mode verdicts answered locally by bili (zero upstream traffic)
en.det.auto_mode_forge_tip: This session's auto-mode safety verdicts are answered locally by bili — no upstream model call, zero billing (#2740)
en.det.calib_tip: Calibration factor ku0302: mean of the last {n} consistent samples (spread {spread}×) on this route+model; deflates estimates only; relearned after a route or model change. Source {origin}{model}.
en.det.ce_comp_hint: Tip: lowering compress.preserveRecentMessages (the protected recent-message count) reduces this — minimum 1
en.det.conflicts_hint: Evidence another compressor touched this session (diagnostic, not history)
en.det.covlost_sub: {n} fold(s) coverage-lost ({x} frozen): their covered messages left the resent history — accrual stopped
en.det.ctx_age_tip: When this context number was measured/estimated; it stops refreshing on restore or idle — an old snapshot is not the current sent view
en.det.handoff_hint: Same content as bili export — paste into a new session to continue
en.det.key_events_tip: Credential fingerprint change = the relay rotated to a different account; fingerprints are 12-hex sha256 prefixes, never raw keys
en.det.ledger_gap_tip: The hit/miss ledger only covers requests since its last (re)build point; requests outside the window are not counted — common with multiple instances sharing a state directory. Folds inside the gap are also missing from fold economics
en.det.legend_base_est: baseline est. (system prompt & tools, not compressible)
en.det.miss_split_line: missed-token split of the hit rate: new content {n} (−{pn}%) · post-fold rebuild {c} (−{pc}%) · unattributed repay {x} (−{px}%, upstream TTL/eviction/unknown)
en.det.not_found_hint: It may have been deleted or lives outside this data dir
en.det.obudget_degraded: ⚠️ Model {model} has NO known output ceiling: its output budget is raised to {value} tokens (the larger of the client's own estimate and the absolute minimum; no authoritative ceiling to back it), so longer replies may be cut off at the output limit. Declare an output limit for this provider/model in bili config, or set maxTokens on the model in the host profile (#2904/#3071)
en.det.omitted: earliest {n} samples were trimmed at write time: each session keeps only its most recent 4096 cache samples (unrecoverable), so the curve starts at the oldest retained sample
en.det.proj_events_tip: Forwarded-projection fingerprint changed while the canonical incoming system/developer content stayed identical = the proxy itself switched compression mode/projection (e.g. self-heal degrade-to-proxy); fingerprints are 16-hex sha256 prefixes, never raw text (#2867)
en.det.prompt_events_tip: Forwarded-projection fingerprint change WITH the canonical incoming content also changed = the host rewrote its system prompt between requests; fingerprints are 16-hex sha256 prefixes, never raw text (#2350/#2867)
en.det.report_note: title & other PII masked by default
en.det.seam_events_tip: First divergence between consecutive outbound bodies; if reproducible attach bili.log around this time (#1548-family)
en.det.seam_mark_tip: ⚠ CACHE SEAM #{seq} · {at} · hit {hit}% · first divergence ≥{lcp} bytes @ message[{msg}] ({prev}→{cur} msgs)
en.det.self_heal_degrade_to_proxy: plugin lane gone → degraded to proxy mode (tools re-injected)
en.det.self_heal_suppress_nudge: nudge idle loop → suppressed (lifts when compression resumes)
en.det.self_heal_tip: Stuck-session self-heal has taken over — see session detail (#2155)
en.det.stab_gap: inter-request gap median: low-hit(<80%) {a}s vs high-hit {b}s
en.det.stab_tip: SHA-256 byte comparison of each outbound body against the previous settled request: identical = byte-exact (e.g. transport retry); diverged pairs classified by first divergence — head <1KiB = host-side parameter change (model/tools/sampling), tail-append = pure tail growth, mid-history = a real prefix rewrite, tail = trailing top-level params or ephemeral tail notes at/past the message-array end (history bytes untouched, cache unaffected), offset-unknown = bodies above the retention cap (inequality still proven by digest)
en.det.traj_zoom_hint: Drag across the chart to zoom into a sample range; double-click or press Esc to reset
en.det.trajectory_empty: No usage samples for this session yet
en.det.trajectory_sub: Per-request input tokens and cache hits; red marks are compression folds
en.det.upper_bound: bound {v} (char-count upper bound — safety protection only, not actual usage)

en.pck.hint: This upstream rejected requests carrying prompt_cache_key (400 with the key, accepted without it), so bili withholds the key there until restart. If this is your relay/account pool, prefix-cache affinity may degrade for those sessions.
en.pluginadv.desc: This plugin re-sends the entire conversation to the model before every tool call for review, so the upstream prefix cache almost never applies (hit rate usually single-digit %) and token cost grows sharply. This is unrelated to bili's compression: bili isolates such requests into a separate sub-session, leaving the main session's prefix cache intact.
